text: respectful constructive. Focus critique ideas implementation details. Assume good intent, ask clarifying questions escalating. Accept responsibility correct mistakes identified.

Facet-level #> sample sizes met the package's `standard` band (smallest level N = 38), an mfrmr-specific #> watermark adapted from Linacre's (1994) 30/100 guidance; facets were nonetheless estimated #> as fixed effects with sum-to-zero identification (see `facet_small_sample_review()`). title: mfrmr Workflow
text: mfrmr treats MML JML differently purpose. MML integrates person distribution Gauss-Hermite quadrature. mml_engine = "direct" (default) optimizes quadrature-based marginal log-likelihood directly. mml_engine = "em" "hybrid" provide documented EM EM-warm-start routes supported RSM/PCM fits. JML useful JMLE-oriented comparisons analyses avoid parametric person distribution. MML package default supports marginal fixed-calibration follow-response-model population-distribution assumptions defensible. RSM PCM, diagnostics now expose two distinct evidence paths: diagnostic_mode = "legacy" keeps residual/EAP-based stack. diagnostic_mode = "marginal_fit" adds strict latent-integrated screen. diagnostic_mode = "" safest default want inspect views side side. Strict marginal diagnostics screening-oriented. Use summary(diag)$diagnostic_basis separate legacy residual evidence strict marginal evidence rather pooling one decision.

text: function tests whether facet elements (e.g., raters) similar enough treated practically interchangeable, rather merely testing whether differ significantly.  key distinction standard chi-square heterogeneity test: absence evidence difference evidence equivalence. function uses existing facet estimates standard errors diagnostics$measures; re-estimation performed. bundle combines four complementary views: Fixed chi-square test: tests \(H_0\): element measures equal.  non-significant result necessary sufficient interchangeability. reported context, direct evidence equivalence. Pairwise TOST (Two One-Sided Tests): pair elements, tests whether difference falls within \(\pm\)equivalence_bound.  TOST procedure (Schuirmann, 1987) rejects null hypothesis non-equivalence one-sided tests significant level \(\alpha\).  pair declared "Equivalent" TOST p-value < 0.05. BIC-based Bayes-factor heuristic: approximate screening tool (full Bayesian inference) compares evidence common-facet model (elements equal) heterogeneity model (elements differ) via \(\mathrm{BF}_{01} \approx \exp((\mathrm{BIC}_{H_1} -    \mathrm{BIC}_{H_0}) / 2)\) (Kass & Raftery, 1995).  Values > 3 favour common-facet model; < 1/3 favour heterogeneity. ROPE-style grand-mean proximity: proportion element's normal-approximation confidence distribution falls within \(\pm\)equivalence_bound weighted grand mean. descriptive proximity summary, Bayesian ROPE decision rule around prespecified null value. title: Fit new data anchored to a baseline calibration — anchor_to_baseline
text: function automates baseline-anchored calibration workflow: Extracts anchor values baseline fit using make_anchor_table(). Re-estimates model new_data anchors fixed via fit_mfrm(..., anchors = anchor_table). Runs diagnose_mfrm() anchored fit. Computes element-level differences (new estimate minus baseline estimate) every common element. model method arguments default baseline fit's settings calibration framework remains consistent.  Elements present anchor table absent new data handled according anchor_policy: "warn" (default) emits message, "error" stops execution, "silent" ignores silently. returned drift table best interpreted anchored consistency check. facet fixed anchor_facets, anchored levels constrained new run, reported differences independent drift analysis. genuine cross-wave drift monitoring, fit waves separately use detect_anchor_drift() resulting fits. Element-level differences calculated every element appears baseline new calibration: $$\Delta_e = \hat{\delta}_{e,\text{new}} - \hat{\delta}_{e,\text{base}}$$ element flagged \(|\Delta_e| > 0.5\) logits \(|\Delta_e / SE_{\Delta_e}| > 2.0\), \(SE_{\Delta_e} = \sqrt{SE_{\mathrm{base}}^2 + SE_{\mathrm{new}}^2}\).

what: Apply empirical-Bayes shrinkage to fitted non-person facet estimates — apply_empirical_bayes_shrinkage
title: Apply empirical-Bayes shrinkage to fitted non-person facet estimates — apply_empirical_bayes_shrinkage
text: Post-hoc shrinkage helper augments mfrm_fit James-Stein / empirical-Bayes shrunk estimates non-person facet. shrinkage variance \(\hat{\tau}^2\) estimated method moments facet-level point estimates standard errors: $$\hat{\tau}^2 = \max\!\left(0,   \frac{1}{K}\sum_{j=1}^{K}\hat{\delta}_j^{2} -   \overline{\mathrm{SE}^2}\right),$$ first term population variance facet point estimates around known mean zero (mfrmr sum--zero identification pins facet mean exactly 0, degree freedom consumed mean estimation). shrinkage factor \(B_j = \mathrm{SE}_j^2 / (\hat{\tau}^2 + \mathrm{SE}_j^2)\), shrunk point / standard error \(\hat{\delta}_j^{EB} = (1 - B_j)\hat{\delta}_j\) \(\mathrm{SE}_j^{EB} = \sqrt{(1 - B_j)\mathrm{SE}_j^2}\). posterior SE form treats \(\hat{\tau}^2\) known; omits Morris (1983, eqs. 4.1-4.2, p. 51) confidence-interval correction \(v \cdot \hat{\delta}_j^{2}\) \(v = 2 B_j^2 / (K - r - 2)\), \(r\) number regression coefficients used model prior mean (mfrmr's sum--zero pinning, \(r = 0\), divisor \(K - 2\)). correction adds variance proportional squared deviation \(\hat{\delta}_j^{2}\), accounting uncertainty \(\hat{\tau}^2\). equal-variance assumption \(\hat{\delta}_j^{2} \approx \hat{\tau}^2\), omitted variance order \(2 / (K - 2)\) times reported posterior variance \(V(1 - B_j)\), true SE approximately \(\sqrt{1 + 2/(K - 2)}\) times reported ShrunkSE. Magnitudes: SE understated ~73\ \(K = 8\), ~7\ ShrunkSE lower bound rather calibrated posterior SE.

Use report screening / triage table; inferential claims hinge marginally-significant -facet contrast, follow contrast uses full parameter covariance.

Elements whose per-link residual exceeds drift_threshold flagged $element_detail$Flag.  high Offset_SD, many flagged elements, thin retained anchor set signals unstable link may compromise resulting scale placement.

text: $links: one row per adjacent pair , , N_Common, N_Retained, Offset_Prelim, Offset, Offset_SD, Max_Residual. Small Offset_SD relative offset indicates consistent shift across elements. LinkSupportAdequate = FALSE means least one linking facet retained fewer 5 common elements screening. $cumulative: one row per wave cumulative offset Wave 1. Wave 1 always offset 0. $element_detail: per-element linking statistics (estimate wave, difference, residual mean offset, flag status). title: Review per-facet-level sample adequacy — facet_small_sample_review
text: "sparse" (n < 10): level-level estimate unstable; SE wide; consider combining adjacent levels treating exploratory . "marginal" (10 <= n < 30): Linacre (1994) 95% CI +-1.0 logit threshold; usable screening . "standard" (30 <= n < 50): meets baseline stability; reasonable publication fit statistics acceptable. "strong" (n >= 50): well-targeted; facet estimate robust. mfrmr shrinkage default, sparse marginal levels "borrow strength" levels. Jones Wind (2018) report rater estimates particularly sensitive thin linking; Facet = "Person" row usually less concern person prior integrates uncertainty.

Historical display columns Fair(M) Average Fair(Z) Average retained compatibility, package-native aliases AdjustedAverage, StandardizedAdjustedAverage, ModelBasedSE, FitAdjustedSE appended formatted outputs. Rasch-family RSM / PCM branch, tables follow standard FACETS Linacre construction: fair averages Rasch-measure--score transformations evaluated standardized mean/zero-facet environment. Bounded GPCM fits supported slope-aware element-conditional construction. slope-facet element \(j^\star\) per-row fair-average GPCM expected score $$\mathrm{FA}_{p, j^\star} = \sum_k k \cdot P_{GPCM}(X = k \mid \theta_p, a_{j^\star}, \boldsymbol{\delta}_{j^\star})$$ computed element's discrimination \(a_{j^\star}\) threshold structure. Rows non-slope facets (Person, Rater, ...) use geometric-mean-one slope GPCM identification convention, rows remain continuous standard PCM Linacre fair-average reduce exactly slopes equal one. identification-based reporting convention package's bounded GPCM route, unique free-discrimination score-side analogue FACETS fair averages. report FACETS score-side equivalence operational scoring rule unless convention substantively justified. Standard errors fair-average value opt-MML bounded GPCM fits via fair_se = TRUE. original SE, Model S.E., ModelBasedSE, Real S.E., FitAdjustedSE columns retain meaning PCM (scaled facet-measure SEs); fair-average uncertainty reported distinct columns Fair(M) S.E., Fair(M) CI Lower, AdjustedAverageSE.

title: Extract model-estimated facet interaction effects — interaction_effect_table
text: mfrmr supports two-way interactions non-person facets, example facet_interactions = "Rater:Criterion". interaction matrix identified zero marginal sums across participating facets, interaction estimates separable two main effects. Positive values indicate higher--expected scores facet-level combination additive model; negative values indicate lower--expected scores. Use table confirmatory model review specifying facet pair substantive interest. exploratory screening without adding parameters fitted model, use estimate_bias() estimate_all_bias().

title: Build an inter-rater agreement report — interrater_agreement_table
text: pairs data.frame contains: Rater1, Rater2 Rater pair identifiers. N Number matched-context observations pair. Exact Proportion exact score agreements. ExpectedExact Model-implied expected exact agreement two raters' fitted category-probability vectors. NA probabilities unavailable. Adjacent Proportion adjacent (+/- 1 category) agreements. MeanDiff Signed mean score difference (Rater1 - Rater2). MAD Mean absolute score difference. Corr Pearson correlation paired scores. Flag Logical; TRUE Exact < exact_warn Corr < corr_warn. OpportunityCount, ExactCount, ExpectedExactCount, AdjacentCount Raw counts behind agreement proportions. summary data.frame contains: RaterFacet Name rater facet analyzed. TotalPairs Number rater pairs evaluated. ExactAgreement Mean exact agreement across pairs. AgreementMinusExpected Observed exact agreement minus expected exact agreement. MeanCorr Mean pairwise correlation. FlaggedPairs, FlaggedShare Count proportion flagged pairs. RaterSeparation, RaterReliability Severity-spread indices rater facet, reported separately agreement.

title: Build report-ready output from mfrm_results() — mfrm_report
text: intended workflow : Create res <- mfrm_results(fit, include = ...). Inspect summary(res)$triage summary(res)$next_actions. Create report <- mfrm_report(res, style = "qc"). Read summary(report) report$first_screen opening detailed report tables. Use report$report_index choose next PrimaryTable, TemplateTable, plot route, export route. Use report$template_index copying APA/QC/validation wording. Use style = "apa", "validation", "reviewer", "technical" reporting question needed. Report rows deliberately distinguish evidence claims. first_screen table compact entry point: gives overall row one row per major evidence area status, readiness, main issue, next action, primary route. summary.mfrm_report method summarizes first screen immediate actions, optional -requested sections, claim-readiness counts, report gaps, template-boundary rows without introducing new pass/fail decision. default print method follows short reading order print every detailed evidence table. HTML output places reader guidance report-summary tables full Markdown text browser view starts first-screen route. report_index table detailed evidence-route index: lists major report areas, evidence status, readiness label, review-signal count, primary/template tables, evidence routes, template routes, plot routes, export route, mfrm_results(include = ...) preset inspect next. ordinary use, open detailed tables PrimaryTable TemplateTable columns rather scanning every element report$tables. template_index table stacks fit, precision, bias, misfit, linking wording templates single boundary/claim-strength index users drill area-specific template tables. claim_readiness table marks report claims ready, caveated, unavailable, require additional requested sections. report_gaps table turns statuses follow-actions. fit-specific tables keep multiple MnSq threshold profiles, observed fit-status counts, engine-vs-FACETS-style ZSTD conventions visible, including small-df/capping boundary used FACETS-style ZSTD review. summarize stored fit_measures component mfrm_results(); mfrm_report() recompute diagnostics. fit_reporting_templates table turns counts cautious reporting language keeping MnSq, ZSTD standardization, df sensitivity, separation/reliability separate sentences. reporting-template tables share EvidenceTable, EvidenceRoute, BoundaryType, ClaimStrength, RecommendedUse columns template can traced back evidence claim boundary. default RecommendedUse "report_with_context"; restrictive rows request evidence, identify methods appendix caveat, require targeted follow-. template_index stacks columns across template areas report authors can review unsupported caveated wording opening full template text. precision_reporting_templates table separation, reliability, strata using stored precision review diagnostics$reliability. bias_reporting_templates table available source result built include = "bias" keeps facet-level screens, interaction-bias contrasts, DFF follow-, fairness conclusions separate lanes. misfit_reporting_templates table available source result built include = "misfit_review" keeps unexpected responses, displacement, pathway-map evidence, case-review actions separate. linking_reporting_templates table available source result built include = "linking" keeps anchor readiness, drift review, equating-chain review, GPCM support boundaries separate. example, fit separation collapsed single pass/fail statement; bias screens treated final fairness conclusions; pathway/misfit rows case-review prompts; drift/equating claims require multiple fitted forms waves.

## Narrative
- Quality-control triage before manuscript, appendix, or reviewer handoff. The report is generated from an existing mfrm_results object and does not refit the model.
- The source result uses model RSM with method JML and 96 observations.
- Highest-priority first-screen signals: Diagnostics=review (diagnostic_warnings_present); Data review=ok (data_readiness_pass); Design / connectivity=ok (design_linked).
- Use the section plan and evidence-boundary table to decide what can be written now, what needs a targeted follow-up helper, and what should remain caveated.

| Wilson-Hilferty ZSTD | (MnSq^(1/3) - (1 - 2 / (9 * df))) / sqrt(2 / (9 * df)). | Requires finite positive MnSq and usable df; small df can dominate the transformation. | ZSTD is a standardization of MnSq, not a separate residual-fit statistic. | Wilson-Hilferty cube-root approximation used in Rasch fit standardization. | fit_measures_table(..., fit_df_method = "engine" or "facets") |
| WHEXACT / linear approximation | (MnSq - 1) * sqrt(df / 2) when whexact = TRUE. | Still requires usable df; use only when the analysis intentionally follows that convention. | State the transformation setting before interpreting ZSTD. | Winsteps/FACETS WHEXACT documentation. | diagnose_mfrm(..., whexact = TRUE) |
| Report comparison route | Keep engine and FACETS-style columns side by side with fit_df_method = "both". | Compare MnSq first, then df, then ZSTD; classify flag changes as convention-sensitive. | Do not explain fit decisions from ZSTD alone when MnSq, df, or threshold profile differs. | facets_fit_df_guide(); facets_fit_review(); fit_measures_table(). | fit_measures_table(..., fit_df_method = "both") |

## Fit Decision Policy
| Step | Rule | Rationale | RecommendedRoute | ReportBoundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Choose and state the MnSq band | Published bands differ by setting; the active band and sensitivity profiles should both be visible. | fit_measures_table(threshold_profiles = "all") | Do not silently mix bands across reports. |
| 2 | Read MnSq before ZSTD | MnSq is the size of the fit signal; ZSTD is a df-dependent standardization of that signal. | fit_measures_table()$table[, c("Infit", "Outfit", "FitStatus")] | Do not treat ZSTD as independent evidence from MnSq. |
| 3 | Keep ZSTD convention visible | FACETS-style df can change \|ZSTD\| flags even when MnSq is unchanged. | fit_measures_table(fit_df_method = "both")$df_sensitivity | Do not call a df-sensitive ZSTD change a substantive fit change without MnSq/context evidence. |
| 4 | Separate fit from precision | Fit, separation, reliability, and strata answer different questions. | precision_review_report()$fit_separation_basis | Do not use high reliability to excuse misfit or good fit to imply high precision. |
| 5 | Treat profile disagreement as sensitivity evidence | A row can be flagged under one defensible band and not another; report this as a review sensitivity. | fit_measures_table()$profile_summary_by_facet | Do not present one threshold profile as universal. |
| 6 | Use local review before action | Element fit flags are prompts for inspecting responses, raters, items, categories, or design links. | unexpected_response_table(); displacement_table(); plot(res, type = "pathway") | Do not remove levels or observations from fit flags alone. |

| Category functioning | Describe how score categories function and where thresholds or curves need review. | Standalone validity evidence. | rating_scale_table(); category_structure_report(); category_curves_report() |

text: Marginal Maximum Likelihood (MML) MML integrates person ability distribution using Gauss-Hermite quadrature, broader marginal-likelihood framework introduced Bock & Aitkin (1981) IRT: $$L = \prod_{n} \int P(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta, \boldsymbol{\delta})   \, \phi(\theta) \, d\theta   \approx \prod_{n} \sum_{q=1}^{Q} w_q \,   P(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta_q, \boldsymbol{\delta})$$ \(\phi(\theta)\) assumed normal prior \((\theta_q, w_q)\) quadrature nodes weights.  Person estimates obtained post-hoc via Expected Posteriori (EAP): $$\hat{\theta}_n^{\mathrm{EAP}} =   \frac{\sum_q \theta_q \, w_q \, L(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta_q)}        {\sum_q w_q \, L(\mathbf{X}_n \mid \theta_q)}$$ MML estimate one fixed person parameter per respondent therefore avoids JML incidental-parameter mechanism. structural inference nevertheless conditional specified population distribution, response model, quadrature approximation, regularity conditions; automatic small-sample guarantee. Note: Bock & Aitkin (1981) canonical citation Gauss-Hermite-quadrature MML framework. default mfrmr engine (mml_engine = "direct") optimises marginal log-likelihood direct gradient methods (BFGS / L-BFGS-B), Bock & Aitkin's signature EM algorithm. "em" "hybrid" engines follow EM template use selected gradient-based M-step rather B&'s probit IRLS, target polytomous Rasch family rather B&'s 2PL probit model. Joint Maximum Likelihood (JML) JML estimates person facet parameters simultaneously fixed effects maximising joint log-likelihood \(\ell(\boldsymbol{\theta}, \boldsymbol{\delta} \mid \mathbf{X})\) directly.  assume parametric person distribution, can advantageous population shape strongly non-normal. incidental-parameter concern simply small-person-sample issue: structural-parameter bias can persist number persons increases number ratings items per person remains fixed (Neyman & Scott, 1948). package still accepts "JMLE" backward-compatible alias, user-facing summaries documentation use "JML" public label. pair with pathway when category behavior is central. #> 5        Main text when precision or targeting across theta is a substantive claim. #>                                                                                   WhatToReport #> 1      Describe whether persons, facet levels, and thresholds overlap on the same logit scale. #> 2         Describe expected-score progression and the theta regions where categories dominate. #> 3 Describe whether categories peak in the intended order and whether adjacent curves separate. #> 5                   Describe where measurement information is highest or weakest across theta. #>                                                                                                                 CaptionSkeleton #> 1           Figure X. Wright map showing person measures, facet-level locations, and step thresholds on the shared logit scale. #> 2                    Figure X. Expected score pathway across theta, with dominant-category regions for the fitted rating scale. #> 3                                  Figure X. Category characteristic curves showing fitted category probabilities across theta. #> 5 Figure X. Test information curve showing where the fitted model provides relatively stronger or weaker measurement precision. #>                                                                                                                       ResultsWording #> 1           The Wright map was inspected to evaluate targeting and shared-scale overlap among persons, facet levels, and thresholds. #> 2 The pathway plot was inspected to evaluate whether expected scores and dominant-category regions progressed in the intended order. #> 3           The category characteristic curves were inspected to evaluate the ordering and separation of fitted response categories. #> 5            The information curve was inspected to identify theta regions with relatively stronger or weaker measurement precision. #>                                                                                            WhatNotToClaim #> 1                                                  Do not present targeting as proof of global model fit. #> 2                       Do not treat smooth category progression as proof that the rating scale is valid. #> 3 Do not overstate overlapping curves as definitive category failure without category counts and context. #> 5                    Do not ignore the precision tier or approximation caveats used to compute the curve. #>                                                               BeginnerCheck #> 1            Check gaps between person density and thresholds/facet levels. #> 2 Check whether the dominant-category bands progress in the expected order. #> 3   Check whether every retained category has a visible peak or clear role. #> 5   Check whether the information peak covers the theta region of interest. #>                                                 ThreeDPolicy #> 1            2D recommended; title: Plot parameter-recovery simulation results — plot.mfrm_recovery_simulation
text: x Output evaluate_mfrm_recovery(). y Reserved S3 generic compatibility. type Plot route: "summary" draws metric x$recovery_summary, "coverage" draws 95% coverage parameter group, "errors" draws row-level recovery-error distributions, "scatter" draws truth estimated values, "replications" summarizes run status. metric Summary metric used type = "summary". Supported values "rmse", "bias", "mae", "correlation", "coverage", "mcse_bias", "mcse_rmse", "raw_rmse", "raw_bias", "mean_se", "se_available". parameter_type Optional parameter type filter, "person", "facet", "step", "slope", "population". facet Optional facet filter. comparison Error/estimate scale row-level routes. "aligned" uses EstimateAligned / ErrorAligned; "unaligned" uses Estimate / ErrorRaw comparison scale. draw TRUE, draw base graphics. FALSE, return mfrm_plot_data object reusable plot tables metadata. ... Reserved generic compatibility.

title: Plot parameter-recovery simulation results — plot.mfrm_recovery_simulation
text: mfrm_plot_data object. draw = TRUE, object returned invisibly drawing.

title: Plot DIF/bias screening simulation results — plot.mfrm_signal_detection
text: x Output evaluate_mfrm_signal_detection(). signal Whether plot DIF bias screening results. metric Metric plot. signal = "bias", prefer metric = "screen_rate" screening hit rate. older metric = "power" spelling retained backwards-compatible alias maps BiasScreenRate. x_var Design variable used x-axis. x generated sim_spec custom public facet names, corresponding aliases (example n_judge, n_task, judge_per_person) also accepted. Role keywords (person, rater, criterion, assignment) accepted abstraction current two-facet schema. group_var Optional design variable used separate lines. alias rules x_var apply. draw TRUE, draw base graphics; otherwise return plotting data. ... Reserved generic compatibility.

title: Plot DIF/bias screening simulation results — plot.mfrm_signal_detection
text: draw = TRUE, invisibly returns plotting data. draw = FALSE, returns plotting-data list directly. returned list includes resolved canonical variables (x_var, group_var) together public labels (x_label, group_label), design_variable_aliases, design_descriptor, planning_scope, planning_constraints, planning_schema, display_metric, interpretation_note callers can label bias-side plots screening summaries rather formal power/error-rate displays.

title: Plot a summary-table bundle for manuscript QC — plot.mfrm_summary_table_bundle
text: "table_rows": compares returned table sizes show reporting mass sits. "role_tables": shows many returned tables belong reporting role. "appendix_roles": shows returned tables contribute conservative appendix routing reporting role. "appendix_sections": shows returned tables distributed across methods/results/diagnostics/reporting sections. "appendix_presets": shows many tables current bundle contributes conservative appendix presets. "selection_handoff_presets": shows plot-ready appendix handoff counts preset workflow-appendix routing surfaces bundle. "selection_tables" / "selection_handoff" / "selection_handoff_bundles" / "selection_handoff_roles" / "selection_handoff_role_sections" / "selection_bundles" / "selection_roles" / "selection_sections": show workflow-appendix selection surfaces already materialized inside bundle. "numeric_profile" / "first_numeric": reuse numeric QC logic plot.apa_table() start summary-table bundle.

title: Plot anchor drift or a screened linking chain — plot_anchor_drift
text: Three plot types supported: "drift" (mfrm_anchor_drift objects): dot plot element's drift value, grouped facet.  Horizontal reference lines mark drift threshold.  Red points indicate flagged elements. "heatmap" (mfrm_anchor_drift objects): wave--element heat matrix showing drift magnitude.  Darker cells represent larger absolute drift.  Useful spotting systematic patterns (e.g., criteria shifting direction). "chain" (mfrm_equating_chain objects): line plot cumulative offsets across screened linking chain. flatter line indicates smaller -wave shifts; steep segments suggest larger link offsets deserve review.

title: Plot anchor drift or a screened linking chain — plot_anchor_drift
text: Use type = "drift" mfrm_anchor_drift object review flagged elements directly. Use type = "heatmap" mfrm_anchor_drift object spot wave--element patterns. Use type = "chain" mfrm_equating_chain object build_equating_chain() inspect cumulative offsets across waves.

text: Drift change element's estimated measure calibration waves, accounting screened common-element link offset. element flagged absolute drift exceeds threshold (typically 0.5 logits) drift--SE ratio exceeds secondary criterion (typically 2.0), ensuring practically noticeable relatively precise shifts flagged. drift heatmap plots, red dark-shaded elements exceed thresholds.  Common causes include rater drift time, item exposure effects, curriculum changes. chain plots, uneven spacing waves suggests differential shifts screened linking offsets. \(y\)-axis shows cumulative logit-scale offsets; flatter segments indicate stable adjacent links. Bubbles above the band are underfit #   (noisy elements); below the band are overfit (overly predictable). # # For the Winsteps Table 30 layout pass `view = "infit_outfit"`: p_io <- plot_bubble(fit, diagnostics = diag, view = "infit_outfit",                      draw = FALSE) p_io$data$view #> [1] "infit_outfit" # Look for: bubbles clustered inside the central [0.5, 1.5] x [0.5, 1.5] #   square. Points outside the upper-right corner have both Infit #   AND Outfit > 1.5 (consistent underfit); points outside the #   lower-left have both < 0.5 (consistent overfit). title: Plot a differential-functioning heatmap — plot_dif_heatmap

title: Plot a differential-functioning heatmap — plot_dif_heatmap
text: x Output dif_interaction_table(), analyze_dff(), analyze_dif(). mfrm_dff/mfrm_dif object passed, cell_table element used (requires method = "residual"). metric metric plot: "obs_exp" observed-minus-expected average (default), "t" standardized residual / t-statistic, "contrast" pairwise differential-functioning contrast (mfrm_dff objects dif_table). draw TRUE (default), draw plot. show_values Logical. TRUE (default), print rounded cell values top heatmap. value_digits Non-negative integer number digits decimal point cell labels. flag_threshold Optional non-negative absolute-value threshold. supplied, cells abs(value) >= flag_threshold recorded $data$flag_matrix outlined drawn heatmap. scale_limit Optional positive scalar symmetric color scale -scale_limit +scale_limit. Use make several heatmaps visually comparable. flag_color Border color cells meeting flag_threshold. ... Additional graphical parameters passed graphics::image().

title: Plot a differential-functioning heatmap — plot_dif_heatmap
text: Invisibly, mfrm_plot_data object whose data slot bundles row x column metric matrix ($matrix), source long table ($pairs), metric label. Earlier 0.1.x releases returned bare matrix; consume $data$matrix keep code forward-compatible.

title: Plot a differential-functioning heatmap — plot_dif_heatmap
text: Warm colors (red) indicate positive Obs-Exp values (model underestimates facet level group). Cool colors (blue) indicate negative Obs-Exp values (model overestimates). White/neutral indicates systematic difference. "contrast" view best pairwise differential-functioning summaries, whereas "obs_exp" "t" best cell-level diagnostics.

title: Plot a differential-functioning heatmap — plot_dif_heatmap
text: Compute interaction dif_interaction_table() differential- functioning contrasts analyze_dff(). Plot plot_dif_heatmap(...). Identify extreme cells contrasts follow-.

title: Plot a differential-functioning heatmap — plot_dif_heatmap
code: # \donttest{ toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")  fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",                  method = "JML", model = "RSM", maxit = 30) #> Warning: Optimization convergence review did not produce an inference-ready numerical solution (code = 1, status = iteration_limit). Optimizer reached the iteration limit before the terminal gradient became small enough for review-only acceptance. Inspect the model specification, data support, and starting values. Do not interpret estimates until the review is resolved. diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none") int <- dif_interaction_table(fit, diag, facet = "Rater",                              group = "Group", data = toy, min_obs = 2) heat <- plot_dif_heatmap(int, metric = "obs_exp", draw = FALSE) dim(heat$data$matrix) #> [1] 4 2 # Look for (`metric = "obs_exp"`): cells near 0 are aligned with #   model expectation; |Obs - Exp| > 0.5 logits is a substantive #   gap. With `metric = "t"` the cell scale becomes a standardized #   residual where |t| > 2 is a screening flag, not a standalone #   hypothesis test. With `metric = "contrast"` the layout switches #   to Level x GroupPair and reads as the pairwise differential- #   functioning contrast (use `analyze_dff()`). # }

title: Plot displacement diagnostics using base R — plot_displacement
text: Displacement quantifies much single element's calibration shift overall model allowed move freely. computed : $$\mathrm{Displacement}_j = \frac{\sum_i (X_{ij} - E_{ij})}                                      {\sum_i \mathrm{Var}_{ij}}$$ sums run observations involving element \(j\). standard error \(1 / \sqrt{\sum_i \mathrm{Var}_{ij}}\), t-statistic \(t = \mathrm{Displacement} / \mathrm{SE}\) flags elements whose observed residual pattern inconsistent current anchor structure. Displacement informative anchoring: large values suggest anchored values may drifting current sample. non-anchored analyses, displacement reflects residual calibration tension.

title: Plot displacement diagnostics using base R — plot_displacement
text: "lollipop" (default) Dot--line chart displacement values. X-axis: displacement (logits).  Y-axis: element labels.  Points colored red flagged (default: \(|\mathrm{Disp.}| > 0.5\) logits).  Dashed lines \(\pm\) threshold.  Ordered absolute displacement. "hist" Histogram displacement values Freedman-Diaconis breaks.  Dashed reference lines \(\pm\) threshold.  Use inspecting overall distribution shape.

title: Plot displacement diagnostics using base R — plot_displacement
text: Lollipop: top absolute displacement levels; flagged points indicate larger movement anchor expectations. Histogram: overall displacement distribution threshold lines. symmetric distribution centred near zero indicates good anchor stability; heavy tails skew suggest systematic drift. Use anchored_only = TRUE main question anchor robustness.

text: Run plot_type = "lollipop" anchored_only = TRUE. Inspect distribution plot_type = "hist". Drill flagged rows via displacement_table().

title: Plot facet-equivalence results — plot_facet_equivalence
text: forest plot, shaded band marks ROPE (\(\pm\)equivalence_bound around weighted grand mean). Levels whose entire confidence interval lies inside band close facet grand mean descriptive screen. Levels whose interval extends outside band displaced facet average. Overlapping intervals two elements suggest reliably separable, overlap alone establish formal equivalence—use TOST results . ROPE bar chart, bar shows proportion element's normal-approximation distribution falls inside ROPE-style grand-mean proximity.  Values > 95\ element's normal-approximation uncertainty falls near facet average; 50–95\ meaningfully displaced average.

text: Inter-rater agreement plots summarize pairwise consistency chosen rater facet.  Agreement statistics computed observations share person context-facet levels, ensuring comparisons reflect identical rating targets. Exact agreement proportion matched observations raters assigned category score.  expected agreement line shows proportion expected chance given rater's marginal category distribution, providing baseline. Low correlations suggest inconsistent rank ordering persons raters. "difference" Scatter plot.  X-axis: mean signed score difference (Rater 1 \(-\) Rater 2); positive values indicate Rater 1 severe. title: Plot a base-R QC dashboard — plot_qc_dashboard
text: Recommended panel order fast review: Category counts + Infit/Outfit (row 1): first-pass model screening. Category bars roughly track expected line; Infit/Outfit points often reviewed heuristic 0.5–1.5 band. Unexpected responses + Displacement (row 2): element-level outliers.  Sparse points small displacements desirable. Inter-rater + Chi-square (row 3): facet-level comparability. Read screening panels: higher agreement suggests stronger scoring consistency, significant fixed chi-square indicates detectable facet spread current model. Separation/Reliability (row 3): approximate screening precision. Higher separation indicates statistically distinct strata current SE approximation. Treat dashboard screening layer; follow dedicated helpers (plot_unexpected(), plot_displacement(), plot_interrater_agreement(), plot_facets_chisq()) detailed diagnosis.

text: Two plot types provided visual triage QC results: "traffic_light" (default): horizontal bar chart one row per QC check.  Bars coloured green (Pass), amber (Warn), red (Fail).  Provides --glance summary current QC review state. "detail": panel showing check's observed value pass/warn/fail thresholds.  Useful understanding close borderline result next verdict level.

title: Plot QC pipeline results — plot_qc_pipeline
text: pipeline evaluates 10 checks (depending available diagnostics): Convergence: optimizer converge? Overall Infit: global information-weighted mean-square Overall Outfit: global unweighted mean-square Misfit rate: proportion elements \(|\mathrm{ZSTD}| > 2\) Category usage: minimum observations per score category Disordered steps: whether threshold estimates monotonic Separation (per facet): element discrimination adequacy Residual PCA eigenvalue: first-component eigenvalue (computed) Displacement: maximum absolute displacement across elements Inter-rater agreement: minimum pairwise exact agreement

title: Plot QC pipeline results — plot_qc_pipeline
text: Green (Pass): check meets current threshold-profile criteria. Amber (Warn): borderline—monitor necessarily disqualifying.  Review detail panel see close value fail threshold. Red (Fail): requires investigation strong operational interpretive claims made current run. Common remedies include collapsing categories (disordered steps), removing outlier raters (misfit), increasing sample size (low separation). detail view shows numeric values, making easy communicate exact results stakeholders.

title: Simulate long-format ordered many-facet data for design studies — simulate_mfrm_data
text: n_person Number persons/respondents. n_rater Number rater facet levels. n_criterion Number criterion/item facet levels. raters_per_person Number raters assigned person. design Optional named design override supplied named list, named vector, one-row data frame. sim_spec = NULL, names may use canonical variables (n_person, n_rater, n_criterion, raters_per_person) role keywords (person, rater, criterion, assignment). nested named-facet form, design$facets = c(person = ..., rater = ..., criterion = ...), also accepted supported person/rater/criterion design. specify variable design scalar count arguments. score_levels Number ordered score categories. theta_sd Standard deviation simulated person measures. rater_sd Standard deviation simulated rater severities. criterion_sd Standard deviation simulated criterion difficulties. noise_sd Optional observation-level noise added linear predictor. step_span Spread step thresholds logit scale. group_levels Optional character vector group labels. supplied, balanced Group column added simulated data. dif_effects Optional data.frame describing true group-linked DIF effects. Must include Group, least one design column Criterion, numeric Effect. interaction_effects Optional data.frame describing true non-group interaction effects. Must include least one design column Rater Criterion, plus numeric Effect. seed Optional random seed. model Measurement model recorded simulation setup. current public generator supports RSM, PCM, bounded GPCM. step_facet Step facet used model = "PCM" threshold values vary across levels. Currently "Criterion" "Rater" supported. slope_facet Slope facet used model = "GPCM". current bounded GPCM branch requires slope_facet == step_facet. thresholds Optional threshold specification. Use numeric vector common thresholds; named list list(C01 = c(-1, 0, 1)); numeric matrix one row per StepFacet one column per step; long data frame columns StepFacet, Step/StepIndex, Estimate. slopes Optional slope specification used model = "GPCM". Use either numeric vector aligned generated slope-facet levels data frame columns SlopeFacet Estimate. Supplied slopes treated relative discriminations normalized package's geometric-mean-one identification convention log scale. omitted, slopes default 1 every slope-facet level, giving exact PCM reduction. assignment Assignment design. "crossed" means every person sees every rater; "rotating" uses balanced rotating subset; "resampled" reuses person-level rater-assignment profiles stored sim_spec; "sparse_linked" uses incomplete rating design optional linking persons; "skeleton" reuses observed response skeleton stored sim_spec, including optional Group/Weight columns available. omitted, function chooses "crossed" raters_per_person == n_rater, otherwise "rotating". sparse_controls Optional named list used assignment = "sparse_linked". Supported entries link_fraction, link_persons, link_raters_per_person, assignment_mode, min_common_persons_per_rater_pair. See build_mfrm_sim_spec() contract. sim_spec Optional output build_mfrm_sim_spec() extract_mfrm_sim_spec(). supplied, defines generator setup; direct scalar arguments treated legacy inputs generally left defaults except seed. custom public two-facet names recorded sim_spec$facet_names also carried simulated output downstream planning helpers. sim_spec stores active latent-regression population generator, returned object also carries generated one-row-per-person background-data table needed refit population model later.

title: Simulate long-format ordered many-facet data for design studies — simulate_mfrm_data
text: long-format data.frame core columns Study, Person, two simulated non-person facet columns, Score. default facet columns Rater Criterion; sim_spec records custom public names, names used instead. group labels simulated reused observed response skeleton, Group column included. weighted response skeleton reused, Weight column also included.

title: Simulate long-format ordered many-facet data for design studies — simulate_mfrm_data
text: function generates synthetic ordered many-facet data RSM, PCM, package's bounded GPCM branch. data-generating process : Draw person abilities: \(\theta_n \sim N(0, \texttt{theta\_sd}^2)\) Draw rater severities: \(\delta_j \sim N(0, \texttt{rater\_sd}^2)\) Draw criterion difficulties: \(\beta_i \sim N(0, \texttt{criterion\_sd}^2)\) Generate evenly-spaced step thresholds spanning \(\pm\)step_span/2 observation, compute linear predictor \(\eta = \theta_n - \delta_j - \beta_i + \epsilon\) \(\epsilon \sim N(0, \texttt{noise\_sd}^2)\) (optional) Compute category probabilities recorded measurement model (RSM, PCM, bounded GPCM) sample response Latent-value generation explicit: latent_distribution = "normal" draws centered normal person/rater/ criterion values using supplied standard deviations latent_distribution = "empirical" resamples centered support values recorded sim_spec$empirical_support sim_spec$population$active = TRUE, person measures generated stored latent-regression population model template person covariates rather theta_sd dif_effects supplied, specified logit shift added \(\eta\) focal group target facet level, creating known DIF signal.  Similarly, interaction_effects injects known bias specific facet-level combinations. generator targets common two-facet rating design (persons \(\times\) raters \(\times\) criteria).  raters_per_person controls incomplete-block structure: less n_rater, person assigned rotating subset raters keep coverage balanced reproducible. Threshold handling intentionally explicit: thresholds = NULL, common equally spaced thresholds generated step_span thresholds numeric vector, used one common threshold set thresholds named list, numeric matrix, data frame, threshold values may vary StepFacet (currently Criterion Rater) bounded GPCM, generator requires explicit slope contract parallel threshold table. supported route keeps slope_facet == step_facet, normalizes supplied slopes geometric-mean-one log-slope identification used fit_mfrm(), samples responses corresponding GPCM category probabilities. Independent arbitrary slope-facet planning supported design, population-forecasting, diagnostic-screening, signal-detection helpers. Assignment handling also explicit: "crossed" uses full person x rater x criterion design "rotating" assigns deterministic rotating subset raters per person "sparse_linked" assigns persons incomplete rater subset assigns configurable set linking persons larger rater set "resampled" reuses empirical person-level rater profiles stored sim_spec$assignment_profiles, optionally carrying person-level Group "skeleton" reuses observed person--rater--criterion response skeleton stored sim_spec$design_skeleton, optionally carrying Group Weight Sparse linked simulation intended planned-missing rating designs connectivity maintained common linking persons. returned mfrm_sparse_design attribute summarizes design density, planned missingness, rater coverage, rater-pair common-person counts. summaries design diagnostics, model-fit statistics universal adequacy thresholds. branch follows sparse rater-mediated assessment design work Wind, Jones, Grajeda (2023, doi:10.1177/01466216231182148), Wind Jones (2018, doi:10.1177/0013164417703733), DeMars, Shapovalov, Hathcoat (2023). controlled workflows, build reusable simulation specification first via build_mfrm_sim_spec() derive one observed fit extract_mfrm_sim_spec(), pass sim_spec. Returned data include attributes: mfrm_truth: simulated true parameters (parameter-recovery checks) mfrm_truth$signals: injected DIF interaction signal tables mfrm_truth$slope_table: simulated discrimination table bounded GPCM mfrm_population_data: generated one-row-per-person background data simulation specification stores active latent-regression generator, including model-matrix xlevel contrast provenance categorical covariates mfrm_simulation_spec: generation settings (reproducibility) mfrm_sparse_design: sparse-design diagnostics assignment = "sparse_linked", including design density, planned missing rate, rater coverage, rater-pair common-person counts

title: Simulate long-format ordered many-facet data for design studies — simulate_mfrm_data
text: Higher theta values mfrm_truth$person indicate higher person measures. Higher values mfrm_truth$facets$Rater indicate severe raters. Higher values mfrm_truth$facets$Criterion indicate difficult criteria. mfrm_truth$signals$dif_effects mfrm_truth$signals$interaction_effects record injected detection targets.
